<a id="architecture"></a>

## Architecture

One query, one function. The nearest CTE in crates/store/src/embeddings.rs builds candidate_vectors by scanning the HNSW index (cheap) and then ADMITTING each candidate through a correlated EXISTS that, for smart vectors, nests a second EXISTS on smart_content — Postgres cannot hash that, so it nested-loops a materialised Seq Scan of elements per candidate and probes smart_content ~1M times. The rewrite resolves the two admission sets ONCE as CTEs — admitted elements (with the caller's filters applied) and a smart_map of (text_hash → raw_hash) — and joins the candidate stream to them with hash semi-joins; the CTE stops carrying vectors. The candidate-expansion loop is untouched but each pass becomes cheap. Evidence altitude: an EXPLAIN-shape test (structural, mutation-checked against the old SQL kept as a golden string), a ranking-parity test against a golden of the old output, then PROD — the profiler's exact query and binds, and wall-clock on the queries that timed out this morning.

<a id="risks"></a>

## Risks

| id | text |
| --- | --- |
| risk-1 | Parity golden captured from a query that is itself wrong in some edge (e.g. double-admission) would freeze the bug — the coder must state any golden row it believes is wrong at ack rather than match it |
| risk-2 | A planner that still chooses a nested loop on a small seeded corpus — the shape test must seed enough rows, or assert on prod-sized stats via pg_stat |
| risk-3 | Filters that were applied inside the correlated EXISTS (kind, gate_open, ddoc_schema, conversation) must be applied to the admitted set with identical semantics — enumerate each in the ack |
| risk-4 | Candidate expansion: if parity requires the same under-fill behaviour, the loop stays; document the pass count for the reference query before/after |
